definition: Making recoverable copies of data, on site, off site or in the cloud. Does not include live replication with failover, or a secondary site for running services.

Continuously replicating data or systems so that services switch to another environment when the primary one fails. Does not include periodic backups or a separate recovery site for restoring services later.
A secondary data centre or environment from which critical services are restored after a disruption. Does not include backups of data alone.
Defined recovery time or recovery point objectives, disaster recovery plans, or tested recovery procedures. Does not include the backup, replication or recovery site itself.
Converting paper records to electronic form, stored and backed up, so that they survive damage to the physical copies in a disaster. Does not include backup of data that is already digital.
Creates recoverable copies of data at the same location
Stores backup copies of data at a separate location or in the cloud
Replicates data, applications or systems across environments
Transfers services to an alternative environment following failure
